title: Head, Innovation Hubs
description: About us Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. About the role Moniepoint is building innovation hubs at three of Nigeria’s leading universities: Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), and Ahmadu Bello University (ABU). Each hub is a cross-disciplinary platform, open to students from every faculty. The model is cohort-based, industry-connected, and built to produce technical talent ready for the job market, across software engineering, AI, product, data science, robotics, and design. The hubs train students in applied technical skills, connect them to working engineers, product leaders, and founders, and provide a path into industry at Moniepoint, at other technology companies, or through ventures of their own. This is a building role. The hubs are entering their operating phase, and you will own the design of how they run and the teams that run them. What you will own Programme design. You will design the operating model for all three hubs from the ground up: how cohorts are structured, how learning is sequenced, what “job market-ready” means at each level, and how graduates are assessed and certified. This is not adapting someone else’s playbook. It is writing one. University relationships. You will be the primary relationship owner with the Vice-Chancellors, deans, faculty leads, and student bodies at OAU, UNN, and ABU. These are institutional relationships that require both strategic seniority and sustained presence. Cross-faculty engagement. The hubs are not engineering faculty initiatives. They are open to students across every faculty: engineering, sciences, humanities, business, design. You will design the engagement model that brings students from across each university into the hub and keeps them in it through the full cohort. Industry and mentorship pipeline. The hubs derive their value from the connection between classroom and industry. You will build and manage the network of engineers, product leaders, and founders, inside Moniepoint and beyond, who mentor, assess, and hire from the hubs. Facilitators and standard.  You will design the facilitator model, recruit the people who teach and assess, and own the standard those facilitators hold the cohort to. A single standard across all three hubs is non-negotiable; how it's delivered locally is yours to design. Infrastructure and operations. You will own the physical footprint of each hub, whether that means a buildout from scratch or working within an existing campus structure, and manage the timelines, vendor relationships, and hub-level budgets across three sites. You will define the staffing model for each hub and recruit the on-ground team that runs them day to day. Outcomes and accountability. You will set and own the metrics: graduate output, job placement, programme completion, cohort quality, employer satisfaction. Pipeline integration. The hubs are upstream of Moniepoint Academy and other talent programmes. You will design the connective tissue between hub graduates and Moniepoint’s internal pathways, so the strongest talent has a clear next step. Who you are 10+ years of experience overall, with at least 5 in leadership roles owning programmes, teams, and budgets end to end. You have built or led a technical training or workforce development programme at scale, ideally across multiple sites. You have taken something from zero to one - designed the model, hired the team, and held the standard yourself. You have held institutional relationships at senior level across universities, government bodies, and industry partners. You know how to navigate Nigerian university administration, or you have done it elsewhere and can credibly do it here. You have hired and managed technical educators, and you know what separates someone who can teach from someone who can teach to a standard. You understand what good engineering education looks like and what employers in software, AI, product, and data science actually hire for. You don't need to write code, but you need the technical fluency to design a programme that produces hireable engineers, not credentialed graduates. You are rigorous about outcomes and impatient with programmes that look good in announcements but cannot prove what they produce. Experience in edtech, developer education, university-industry partnerships, or workforce development is a strong signal. Building something from scratch and owning it through to measurable outcomes is essential. What success looks like Year one. Operating model live across all three hubs. Cohorts running on a common standard. The facilitator team hired and held to the same expectations regardless of site. First graduate cohort exited, with a clear placement record into Moniepoint and into industry. Year two. The hubs are recognised within Nigeria as the most credible cross-disciplinary technical training environment available to undergraduates. Employers, including Moniepoint, actively hire from the hubs. Cohort demand outstrips supply. Year three. Hubs producing technical talent into Moniepoint at a cost-per-hire that justifies the investment, and into the wider industry at a scale and quality that defines what a corporate-funded university programme can look like in Nigeria. Model documented and ready to expand if leadership chooses. What Moniepoint can offer you The opportunity to shape one of the most consequential talent infrastructure investments in Nigerian technology.  A dynamic, diverse, and collaborative environment where every team member's voice is recognised and valued.  Continuous learning and career growth opportunities.  Competitive salary, individual performance bonuses, and firmwide performance bonus. Company-covered health insurance plans. Pension plans. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary conversation with one of our recruiters. An interview with the hiring manager, our Head of Corporate Affairs. A case study or written exercise on operating model design for the hubs. An interview with our Group COO. A final conversation with our CEO.

title: Head of Debt Collections
description: About Moniepoint Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions and process over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. JOB PURPOSE The Head, Debt Collection is a strategic leadership position tasked with the architecture and execution of Moniepoint’s debt collection framework. The primary focus of this role is the minimization of Loss Given Default (LGD) within both the business and consumer lending divisions.   The incumbent will oversee, develop, and implement comprehensive and versatile debt collection strategies designed to manage a diverse portfolio of credit products, ranging from digital-first retail lending to large-ticket corporate financing.   Responsibilities include designing the organizational structure of the debt collection unit and recruiting high-caliber talent. Additionally, specialized expertise in debt litigation and asset recovery will be required to navigate complex cases of delinquency.   A data-driven methodology must be utilized to systematically evaluate the efficacy of recovery tactics and the performance of personnel.   Job Responsibilities  Design and implement a segmented debt collection framework — differentiated by product type, ticket size, and delinquency stage — spanning early-stage soft collections through hardcore legal recovery, restructuring, and write-off pathways. Define the org structure, recruit high-caliber talent, and stand up the operational and systems infrastructure (collections management systems, tracking dashboards, agent/dialer tooling) needed to run recovery at scale. Direct legal recovery strategy for the department — whether executed directly or through instruction of external counsel — ensuring all actions comply with applicable financial regulations and debt collection laws. Manage high-level engagements with external stakeholders, including law enforcement agencies, regulatory bodies, and external counsel, to expedite resolution of non-performing loans (NPLs). Design incentive structures and performance frameworks (KPIs, commission or fee structures) for the collections and recovery network to drive both recovery rate and cost-to-collect efficiency. Continuously train and upskill the collections and recovery network in alignment with collections  strategy and industry best practice. Own collections and recovery performance reporting to senior management, including recovery rate, cost of recovery, and portfolio-level LGD trends, and feed recommendations into credit committee decisions on write-offs and restructuring. Collaborate with credit, legal, risk, and finance to align collections and recovery efforts with underwriting standards and portfolio strategy. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in a relevant field. Minimum 7 years of experience in credit/debt recovery, including senior leadership of a recovery function handling high-value non-performing loans. Demonstrated experience across both high-ticket/corporate recovery (litigation-led, relationship-driven) and high-volume digital/retail collections (analytics-led, behavioral, tech-enabled)  Strong working knowledge of debt recovery laws, banking regulations, and court procedures in Nigeria. Familiarity with digital collections infrastructure and tactics — dialer/CRM systems, SMS/USSD/app-based nudges, propensity-to-pay scoring, and behavioral segmentation for low-ticket, high-volume portfolios. Demonstrated experience designing, building, or scaling a recovery/collections function — including org design, systems and process build-out, and team hiring. Proven experience overseeing recovery operations with national coverage, including a strong network of legal counsel and law enforcement contacts spanning all six geo-political zones in Nigeria — as opposed to experience confined to a single state or region. Excellent negotiation, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial and portfolio data to guide recovery strategy. Relevant Skills Loan Recovery & Collections Strategy (high-ticket and digital/retail) Credit Risk Management Data Analytics, Propensity Scoring & Portfolio Reporting Digital Collections Tools & Automation Negotiation & Conflict Resolution People & Performance Management Organisational Design & Team Build-out What we can offer you Culture -We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with the recruiter An interview with one of our credit business leads A behavioral and technical interview with a member of the Executive team.  Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Head of Engineering, Field Verification
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Why the UK The UK is home to our headquarters where more than 70 team members are based, with team members joining us from companies like Tide, Klarna, Revolut, Capital One, Teya, Wise, Starling, Monzo, and many others! Our London office is located at Sea Containers, just by London Bridge - this is also where a significant number of our most senior leaders sit, which makes it a natural base for a Head of Engineering. So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Field Verification to join us in UK. About The Role Field Verification is how Moniepoint knows that the people and businesses on our platform are real. Every Moniepoint customer, retail and business, requires a completed field verification as part of KYC. The platform coordinates physical, in-person checks — verifying individuals, business owners, business addresses and loan guarantors — and it serves nearly every part of the company: onboarding, loans, compliance and the fraud team. The system works today. A back office gives each business unit visibility and control over its own verification requests. A mobile-friendly web app puts the work in the hands of Field Verification Officers and the cluster leads who manage them across local government areas. An API layer lets other business units push verification requests in and receive results back by webhook, and an assignment algorithm routes each request to an officer close enough to carry it out. We want to be straightforward about the rest. This domain has never had a dedicated engineering leader, and that is the single biggest constraint on it. The team is one lean, cross-functional squad — an Engineering Manager, four engineers and a QA — carrying verification volume for the entire customer base. They have done that impressively well, but running lean means running in keep-the-lights-on mode, and a long list of things that would make this platform substantially better has been waiting for someone to own it. That list is the role. Trip and route management, so an officer can plan an optimal day across several sites rather than making a separate journey for each one — today we pay for a round trip per verification, and the logistics are nowhere near optimal. Capacity management. A native mobile app, wanted for a long time and never resourced. Liveness and identity verification tooling, exposed as APIs the rest of the business can build on. And as Moniepoint expands into markets where identity verification is as difficult as it is in Nigeria, Kenya among them, a platform that works beyond a single country. There is a great deal of room to build here. Whoever takes this on will set the direction rather than inherit someone else's plan, on a system that already carries real weight for the business. As Head of Engineering, Field Verification, your responsibilities will include: Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Field Verification platform end to end, and setting direction for a domain that has been running without dedicated engineering leadership. Moving the platform from keep-the-lights-on operation to deliberate, prioritised development. Leading and growing the existing cross-functional team, and building the organisation out as scope expands. Building the operational efficiency layer — trip and route optimisation, task allocation and capacity management for field officers. Owning the platform's client-facing surface: the APIs and webhooks that other business units integrate with, and the back office those units rely on. Delivering a native mobile experience for field officers. Ensuring verification data is structured, auditable and fit for compliance scrutiny. Building for multi-country expansion as Moniepoint enters new markets. Partnering closely with Product and with the business units that depend on the platform — onboarding, loans, compliance and fraud. Defining architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and hiring and developing engineers and Engineering Managers. Who You Are You have built things yourself, and grew into leadership from there. We are explicit about this: we are not looking for someone who moved into management early and has led from a distance since. We want an engineer who became a leader. You are capable across disciplines. Backend, web and mobile. This platform spans all three and you will need credibility in each — a specialist in one layer will struggle here. You have built platforms, not just products. Systems used by several distinct groups of users and internal business units, with the flexibility to serve requirements you did not anticipate. You are a problem solver first. We would rather have someone adaptable than someone with the exact domain experience. Having built across different industries — fintech, e-commerce, logistics or otherwise — is a positive signal, not a scattered CV. You have 10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with substantial hands-on production engineering and strong backend depth. Our backend environment is Java and Spring Boot. You have at least 5 years of engineering leadership, including managing Engineering Managers. You collaborate well with product and business stakeholders, and can translate operational requirements into engineering solutions. Experience working with location and geospatial data is a strong plus, including map integrations. Experience with route, trip or delivery optimisation is a strong plus. Experience building for compliance — where data must be structured to evidence what was done and when — is a strong plus. Experience with identity, KYC or verification platforms is a plus. None of these four are requirements. Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Why Poland  Poland is a new and deliberate addition to our engineering map. We recently made our first technology hire in the country, and we are looking at Poland as a long-term strategic location for senior hires, particularly within our engineering organisation. Joining now means joining early, and helping shape what our presence here becomes. So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Sales & Marketing Tools, to join us in Poland. About The Role Sales and Marketing Tools owns MonieCRM, the operating system for Moniepoint's 50,000-strong sales network. This is not a CRM we bought — it is a workforce operations platform built entirely in-house for a multi-level field sales hierarchy, and it is how those teams run their day to day: the portfolio of businesses they manage, their own teams, their goals and performance, the physical and digital resources they need in the field, and an emerging AI-assisted support layer. Sixteen capabilities span onboarding and network management, pipeline and portfolio, performance and goals, compensation, and sales experience and support. A significant part of the domain moves money. The platform owns wallets, commission calculation and attribution, cashout and welfare funds for a network that drives the overwhelming majority of company revenue — which makes financial correctness, not just availability, a core engineering requirement of the role. Alongside that, the domain covers partner management, a rewards and retention platform serving tens of millions of users, and our marketing technology stack, including the engineering and customisation of Braze, the platform we use for customer engagement. This means years spent writing Java yourself, not years spent overseeing teams who write it. At least 5 years of experience managing managers — leading an engineering organisation through other engineering leaders, rather than running a single team. You have proven platform engineering experience at scale — building and running complex distributed systems, not feature delivery alone. You have navigated legacy migrations and re-architecture projects at 20M+ user scale. You have strong backend engineering skills in high-throughput, data-intensive distributed systems, and are proficient in Java and Spring Boot. You have managed and developed large engineering teams of 20 or more members. Experience building systems where financial correctness matters — commissions, payouts, wallets, ledgers or equivalent — is a strong advantage. A fintech or payments background is strongly preferred. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets. Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality. Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality. Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early. Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders. No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes. Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not. Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable. What Success Looks Like The domain has clear technical ownership and direction for the first time. The team out of keep-the-lights-on mode and delivering against a prioritised roadmap. Measurable improvement in field officer efficiency — more verifications per trip, lower cost per verification. A native mobile experience shipped for field officers. Verification data that stands up to compliance scrutiny across every business unit the platform serves. The platform ready to support a new market. A team grown beyond its current size, with a strong bench of engineers and managers. Why Join Us A genuinely greenfield mandate on a system that already matters. Every customer Moniepoint onboards passes through this platform. A lean, capable team making outsized impact, and the remit to build the organisation around them. Breadth: backend, web, mobile, location data, compliance and operational optimisation in one domain. Be part of a mission-driven company expanding access to financial services for millions of businesses and individuals. This is not a CRM we bought — it is a workforce operations platform built entirely in-house for a multi-level field sales hierarchy, and it is how those teams run their day to day: the portfolio of businesses they manage, their own teams, their goals and performance, the physical and digital resources they need in the field, and an emerging AI-assisted support layer. Sixteen capabilities span onboarding and network management, pipeline and portfolio, performance and goals, compensation, and sales experience and support. A significant part of the domain moves money. The platform owns wallets, commission calculation and attribution, cashout and welfare funds for a network that drives the overwhelming majority of company revenue — which makes financial correctness, not just availability, a core engineering requirement of the role. Alongside that, the domain covers partner management, a rewards and retention platform serving tens of millions of users, and our marketing technology stack, including the engineering and customisation of Braze, the platform we use for customer engagement. The mandate is modernisation and reliability: re-architecting systems that have grown very quickly and making them dependable at a scale of more than 20 million users. This is a platform engineering and legacy modernisation challenge first and foremost, and prior CRM or SalesTech experience is genuinely not required. Who You Are  You have 10–15 years of overall software engineering experience, with at least 5 years leading engineering teams through growth phases. 5+ years of hands-on, production-level experience writing and shipping Java code as a practising engineer. This means years spent writing Java yourself, not years spent overseeing teams who write it. At least 5 years of experience managing managers — leading an engineering organisation through other engineering leaders, rather than running a single team. You have proven platform engineering experience at scale — building and running complex distributed systems, not feature delivery alone. You have navigated legacy migrations and re-architecture projects at 20M+ user scale. You have strong backend engineering skills in high-throughput, data-intensive distributed systems, and are proficient in Java and Spring Boot. You have managed and developed large engineering teams of 20 or more members. Experience building systems where financial correctness matters — commissions, payouts, wallets, ledgers or equivalent — is a strong advantage. A fintech or payments background is strongly preferred. CRM or SalesTech domain experience is nice to have and explicitly not required. Exposure to customer engagement or marketing automation platforms such as Braze is a plus, but not a requirement. Cultural Alignment As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation. Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets. Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality. Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality. Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early. Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders. No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes. Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not. Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable. What Success Looks Like In The Role Legacy systems modernised and re-architected, with measurable improvement in reliability and performance. Commissions and earnings calculated, attributed and paid accurately and on time, at network scale. A sales and marketing platform that scales with a rapidly growing agent network across multiple markets. Commercial teams able to move faster because the tooling beneath them is dependable. A high-performing engineering team with a strong bench of managers and senior engineers. Why Join Us Own the platform behind the commercial engine of one of Africa's largest digital banks — the system 50,000 people rely on to do their jobs and to get paid. A genuine platform modernisation mandate with the autonomy and backing to see it through. Be part of a mission-driven company impacting millions of businesses and individuals across Africa and beyond. What To Expect In The Hiring Process 60 minute High level System Design round with one of our Engineering Managers. 60 minute Panel Interview with 2 of our Head of Engineering leaders. 30 minutes focused on a technical deep dive into your CV and into a project or system you built in the past. 30 minutes focused on testing for leadership attributes. 60 minute Stakeholder Management Round with one of our Product Heads/VPs, focused on your stakeholder management and collaboration skills with product and business. 60 minute Technical round and Culture fit interview with our Co-founder & Group CTO (the hiring manager). Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates. #LI-Remote

Direct experience running a distributed agent, agency or independent contractor network of significant scale. Strong command of sales analytics: funnel conversion, productivity distribution, cohort based performance. Strong people leadership skills: training, motivating and managing a large field sales team Experience operating in financial services, telecoms, FMCG distribution or another high volume regulated or semi regulated industry. Willingness to travel across regions regularly. Preferred Qualifications Experience in banking, payments or lending distribution in Nigeria. Experience in building and scaling a field sales team Familiarity with sales enablement tooling and CRM based territory management. You balance empathy with fairness and have strong judgment on what’s “right” versus what’s “easy.” You communicate with clarity and confidence, building trust at every level. You think systemically and you see patterns behind cases and design solutions that prevent recurrence. You value compliance but see your role as enabling business success, not blocking it. An implemented plan to increase agent output, featuring defined benchmarks and measurable tactical growth drivers. Established field sales performance routines, including weekly and monthly reviews, executed against standardized templates with disciplined action tracking. Optimized cost per new active customer, trending within the approved thresholds.

title: Head, POS Recovery
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: POS Recovery Manager Department: POS Channel Reports to: VP, POS Channel About this role: This role owns the end-to-end recovery of non-performing POS terminal assets — from the moment a terminal is flagged as at risk through to physical retrieval, financial settlement, and post-write-off recovery. Responsibilities Recovery Strategy Governance Own the terminal recovery lifecycle that defines escalation speed and settlement windows based on terminal age, transaction history, and recovery economics.  Ensure every terminal that enters recovery mode is assigned, tracked, escalated on schedule, and settled within its gate deadline — recovery, write-off, paid write-off, or insurance claim.  Design and continuously refine the recovery strategy, covering device collection, swap logistics, sales agent coordination, external agency management, and the efficient flow of assets back to custody.  Field Team Leadership Lead, manage, and hold accountable a distributed field recovery team across multiple regions.  Instill a culture of operational discipline, accountability, and ethical conduct. Recovery work involves sensitive situations (confronting custodians about lost assets, handling disputes, managing bounty payments); the team must operate with integrity.  Develop comprehensive standard operating procedures for every recovery scenario: BRM-led recovery, external agency coordination, business takeover, faulty terminal collection, voluntary write-off processing, dispute handling, revive processing.  Build training programmes for recovery agents covering: terminal identification, check-in procedures, evidence collection for disputes, GPS and field management tools, escalation protocols.  KPI Management and Recovery Economics Define and track recovery KPIs: recovery rate (pre-write-off), BRM recovery rate, external recovery rate, average days to recovery, cost per recovery, revive rate (post-write-off), bounty efficiency (bounty spend vs recovery value recovered).  Own the recovery economics: ensure total bounty spend plus logistics cost is always less than the recovery value of the terminals retrieved. The programme must be self-funding — recovery must generate more value than it costs.  Report monthly on: terminals entering recovery mode, terminals recovered, terminals written off, terminals revived, net financial impact, bounty spend, external agency spend, dispute volumes and outcomes.  Experience & Background Minimum 7 years of progressive experience managing large-scale field operations, logistics, asset recovery, or after-sales service, with at least 3 years in a senior leadership role.  Experience managing distributed field teams across multiple regions in Nigeria — you understand the infrastructure, the logistics constraints, and the human dynamics of field recovery operations.  Experience managing third-party service providers, contractors, or agency networks with performance-based contracts.  Direct experience in the Nigerian market with its specific logistical, regulatory, and operational realities.  Preferred: Experience from fintech, telecoms, e-commerce logistics, or any high-volume distributed asset management environment.  Preferred: Experience managing asset recovery at scale (thousands of units per month, not dozens).  Skills & Competencies Proven ability to design and implement structured operational processes (SOPs, escalation frameworks, settlement procedures) from scratch or through a major restructure.  Strong analytical capability — you use data to drive decisions, track performance, calculate ROI on recovery spend.  Financial discipline & budget management — experience managing a budget or cost centre, understanding unit economics, and demonstrating net positive recovery value.  Technical & Systems acumen — experience with product management/development lifecycles (writing briefs, working with engineers), GPS tracking, CRM, field management tools, or route optimisation platforms.  Regulatory & Compliance understanding — familiarity with insurance claim processes, write-off accounting, or asset disposal regulations in Nigeria.  What Success Looks Like in This Role Terminal recovery lifecycle is tightly governed, ensuring swift escalation and settlement within established gate deadlines.  Field recovery operations maintain high ethical standards and operational discipline across all regions.  Recovery program operates as a self-funding unit where total recovery value generated consistently exceeds total bounty and logistics expenditure.  Robust systems, SOPs, and field management tools are seamlessly integrated into daily team operations.  Transparent monthly reporting clearly demonstrates positive net financial impact and high recovery/revive rates.  Why Join Us?  Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.  Support for professional development and a dynamic culture driving financial inclusion across Africa.

title: Inventory Support Officer (Lagos)
description: Who We are Moniepoint Inc is a financial technology company digitizing Africa’s real economy by building a financial ecosystem for businesses, providing them with all the payment, banking, credit and business management tools they need to succeed.  What We do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community, dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We have several products that provide essential services for businesses such as credit, overdrafts etc. We leverage artificial intelligence and data to make our decisions but also have the technology and data-driven best practices used to support our businesses.  1A. Inventory Support Officer – POS Terminals Role Purpose The ISO (Terminals) is the dedicated custodian for all forms of POS terminals flowing through the repair pipeline. The role ensures end-to-end traceability, enforces custody controls, and maintains absolute logical–physical alignment within the Repair Centre's IMS subsystem, covering every stage from receipt of faulty units to dispatch of QA-cleared OK devices. Key Responsibilities Intake & Receipt Management Receive faulty/returned terminals from state offices; verify against the recall waybill at serial-number level before accepting into the IMS. Log all received devices in the IMS with correct status within 24 hours of physical arrival. Identify and quarantine damaged or missing-serial devices; raise a Discrepancy Report immediately. Repair Pipeline Tracking Push faulty devices to technicians daily and update IMS status to 'In Repair' upon assignment. Monitor movement of each terminal through all repair stages: Assessment → In Repair → Awaiting QA → QA Cleared → Dispatch Holding. Enforce the 24–72-hour SLA from receipt-to-assignment and from QA clearance-to-dispatch readiness. QA Integration & Status Management Receive QA-approved terminals and update IMS status to 'QA Cleared – Awaiting Dispatch' within 4 hours. Flag devices that fail QA back to the repair queue or classify as 'Beyond Economic Repair (BER)' with a written justification report. Ensure all 'BER' devices are tagged and isolated in the scrap/disposal holding area. Dispatch & Outbound Logistics Generate the Dispatch List and Waybill for QA-cleared refurbished and OK devices; obtain approval from Repair Centre Manager and Cluster lead before release. Scan all devices at serial level during physical loading; update IMS to 'In Transit – Outbound'. Confirm receipt acknowledgment from the destination state SIO and close the dispatch transaction in IMS. Inventory Counts & Reconciliation Conduct daily physical counts of all terminals in the repair centre; reconcile against IMS records. Escalate any variance (physical vs. logical) to the Lead, Inventory Support within the same business day. Participate in monthly, quarterly, and annual wall-to-wall counts as directed by the Inventory & Warehouse Manager. Compliance & Housekeeping Maintain clearly labelled racks and segregated zones: Faulty, Under-Repair, Refurbished/OK, BER/Scrap. Enforce all provisions of the POS Inventory Control SOP within the repair centre. Uphold audit readiness, workplace safety, and environmental handling standards at all times. Reporting Line Functional: Lead, Inventory Support (Regional) Operational: Repair Centre Manager Dotted: Regional Inventory & Warehouse Manager   1B. Inventory Support Officer – Spare Parts Role Purpose The ISO (Spare Parts) manages the complete lifecycle of all repair consumables — batteries, screens, cables, and accessories — within the repair centre. The role ensures that technicians have the right parts at the right time, waste is minimised, and all issues are fully documented and traceable. Key Responsibilities Spare Parts Receipt & Storage Receive all incoming spare parts consignments; verify at batch/serial level against the accompanying delivery note before logging into IMS. Store spare parts in designated, labelled bins organised by part type and model compatibility. Ensure storage conditions protect electronic components from moisture, dust, and extreme temperature. Issuance Control Issue spare parts ONLY against an approved Job Card raised by a technician and validated by the Repair Centre Manager. Update IMS stock levels immediately upon every issuance; zero unrecorded movements. Manage parts returns from technicians (unused or incorrect parts); update IMS accordingly. Inventory Management & Reconciliation Reconcile physical spare parts stock against IMS records on a weekly basis. Identify slow-moving, expired, or obsolete parts and flag to Lead, Inventory Support. Raise a formal replenishment request when stock falls to the defined reorder threshold. Reporting & Documentation Generate weekly spare parts consumption and stock-position reports for the Lead, Inventory Support. Maintain a complete issuance log linking each spare part to its Job Card and technician. Track Part-Failure data to support procurement and OEM quality feedback. Compliance & Housekeeping Maintain proper zoning, labelling, and cleanliness of the spare parts storage area at all times. Enforce segregation of duty: no self-authorised issuance. Support all scheduled and spot-check inventory counts. Requirements  Minimum of OND in a related discipline  At least 2-year experience in inventory operations. Good computer skills. Must know the Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word and PowerPoint)  Ability to work with limited supervision.  Strong attention to detail and accuracy. Proficiency in inventory management systems and workflow applications. Experience handling large volumes of items  Excellent organizational and record-keeping skills. Effective communication and stakeholder coordination. Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines.

description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.   As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.  transactions in Nigeria.  Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work?  Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth.  About the role  As a Key Account Manager, you will be Moniepoint’s relationship owner for an assigned portfolio of important businesses. You will get to know how each customer operates, build trust with the people who make decisions, and help them get value from Moniepoint’s products. You will monitor account performance, spot risks early and coordinate the right teams to resolve issues. You will also identify opportunities to help customers grow through products that meet their needs. This is a hands-on role that combines customer engagement, field visits, commercial judgment and dependable follow-through.   What you’ll get to do  Build active relationships with assigned businesses and understand their locations, decision makers, priorities, product usage and revenue contribution. Maintain the required contact and visit cadence, recording material conversations, commitments and next steps. Monitor revenue, transaction activity and product usage; investigate unusual changes and raise potential risks early. Keep customers informed during escalations, follow through with the teams responsible and confirm that issues are resolved. Maintain accurate CRM profiles, stakeholder maps, opportunities, risks and action plans. Share useful competitor and market intelligence with your State or Regional Lead. A relevant tertiary qualification or equivalent practical experience. Strong communication, problem-solving and negotiation skills. The ability to take ownership of customer issues and follow through across multiple teams.   Relevant Skills    Key account and relationship management Customer retention and growth Product adoption and opportunity identification Data analysis and CRM management Issue resolution and escalation Stakeholder management Field engagement and customer communication   What we can offer you  Culture -We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. title: Lead, Compliance Quality Assurance
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: Lead, Compliance Quality Assurance Department: Regulatory Compliance  Reports to: Head, Compliance Quality Assurance About this role As the Lead, Compliance Quality Assurance, you are the tactical backbone of our quality assessment framework. You will spearhead the day-to-day operations of our QA Assessor team, transforming quality assurance into a catalyst for operational excellence. Through rigorous standard enforcement and precision-based calibration, you will ensure that Moniepoint’s critical divisions including KYC/Due Diligence, AML, LEA, Transaction Monitoring, and Fraud consistently meet SLAs and regulatory policy standards. Acting as the final line of defense against compliance drift, you are dedicated to maintaining flawless execution, high-velocity accuracy, and total regulatory integrity across all operational touchpoints. Responsibilities Supervise, train, and manage QA Assessors, ensuring consistent grading and execution through regular file calibration exercises.  Lead the secondary review process across the 'Six Pillars' (AML/Transaction Monitoring, Regulatory Control/LEA, and Forensic Fraud), identifying vulnerabilities in accuracy, speed, and regulatory compliance.  Maintain a centralized Compliance Defect Log and translate QA findings into actionable weekly feedback for operational Team Leads to drive continuous improvement.  Perform deep-dive analyses on compliance misses to differentiate between system threshold errors and investigator oversight, recommending necessary process adjustments.  Assist in coordinating internal and external audits by providing evidence of QA testing integrity and ensuring high-quality, audit-ready data. Experience & Background 2–4 years of progressive experience in Compliance QA, Financial Crime Investigation, or EDD/CDD within a FinTech, or commercial bank.  Must have at least 2 years of experience in a supervisory or team lead capacity.  Bachelor’s degree in Law, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field. Skills & Competencies Advanced proficiency in Compliance tools and data analysis using SQL and Excel.  Comprehensive understanding of Nigerian regulatory frameworks (AML/CFT), instant payment fraud, card/POS fraud typologies, and legal protocols for handling Law Enforcement Agency (LEA) and CDD, EDD and Customer screening.  Professional certification such as DCP, CAMS, CFE, or ICA International Diploma is an added advantage. What success looks like in this role Maintenance of flawless execution, high-velocity accuracy, and total regulatory integrity across all operational touchpoints.  Consistent meeting of SLAs and regulatory policy standards across KYC/Due Diligence, AML, LEA, Transaction Monitoring, and Fraud divisions.  Prevention of compliance drift through rigorous standard enforcement and precision-based calibration.  Transformation of quality assurance processes into a true catalyst for operational excellence. Why join us Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities. Fully remote work culture and support for professional development.

title: Metadata & Data Lineage Specialist
description: Who we are  Moniepoint is an all-in-one digital financial services platform powering businesses across emerging markets. Since 2019, our technology has enabled over one million businesses to thrive through comprehensive payment, banking, credit, and business management solutions. Operating through its subsidiaries—including Moniepoint MFB and TeamApt Ltd—Moniepoint processes the majority of Nigeria's POS transactions, representing over $170 billion in annualised Total Payment Volume (TPV). Recognised as Africa’s second-fastest-growing fintech platform and named the Most Inclusive Payment Platform by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) in 2022, Moniepoint continues to scale its profitable financial ecosystem. About this role We are looking for a Metadata & Data Lineage Specialist to build out and run the organization's metadata management and data lineage capabilities. You will be the person who makes our data catalogue genuinely useful — helping teams find, trust, and understand the data they are working with, and tracing exactly how that data moves and transforms across our systems. You will take our metadata management and data lineage frameworks from paper to practice: growing coverage, improving quality, automating collection wherever possible, and building lineage that holds up for our most critical data products, regulatory submissions, and business-critical flows. Responsibilities Metadata Management & Data Cataloguing: Maintain and enhance enterprise metadata, developing business glossaries, data definitions, and ownership frameworks within DataHub. Identify gaps and ensure metadata changes align with governance processes. Data Lineage Management: Develop, maintain, and validate end-to-end data lineage for critical data flows, products, reports, and customer journeys across source systems, ETL/ELT pipelines, and downstream consumers. DataHub Platform & Integration: Support the administration and optimisation of DataHub. Configure ingestion workflows, monitor metadata ingestion jobs, and identify opportunities to improve coverage through automation and APIs. Metadata Quality & Governance: Establish metadata quality rules and KPIs. Perform regular assessments to highlight gaps, support data impact assessments, and ensure alignment with enterprise governance policies. Data Classification & Privacy: Apply data classification metadata based on sensitivity and regulatory requirements. Support Risk, Compliance, and InfoSec teams with necessary lineage information for assessments. AI & Advanced Data Discovery: Drive the adoption of AI-assisted metadata management to automate capture, classification, and enrichment. Contribute to the development of semantic models and knowledge graphs. Stakeholder Engagement: Act as a subject matter expert, facilitating workshops and providing guidance to data producers and consumers to improve overall data literacy and DataHub adoption. Experience & Background Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Management, Data Science, Information Systems, Library/Information Science, Engineering, or a related discipline. 3–6+ years of experience in Metadata Management, Data Governance, Data Architecture, or Data Engineering. Demonstrable hands-on experience with Solidatus, Informatica, DataHub, or a comparable enterprise data catalog platform. Practical experience developing end-to-end data lineage across complex data environments. Deep familiarity with modern data architectures (Medallion, Data Mesh, Data Vault 2.0, warehouses, data lakes, cloud platforms). Experience in financial services, fintech, payments, banking, or another highly regulated data environment is highly desirable. Skills & Competencies Strong proficiency working with technical and business metadata, business glossaries, data domains, and data classification. Experience working with relational databases and a solid understanding of SQL and database structures. Knowledge of APIs, ETL/ELT pipelines, and automated metadata integration. Familiarity with AI-assisted metadata management, semantic modelling, ontologies, and knowledge graph concepts. Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to facilitate training and influence adoption. Professional certification in Data Management or Architecture (e.g., DAMA CDMP, CIMP, DCAM) or related platform certifications are advantageous. What success looks like in this role The enterprise data catalogue is accurate, easily discoverable, and heavily utilised by cross-functional teams to understand data assets. End-to-end data lineage is robust, validated, and actively supports critical data products, regulatory submissions, and incident investigations. Metadata collection is highly automated, maintaining strict quality standards and governance controls with minimal manual intervention. Data literacy and platform adoption (DataHub) scale across the organisation through effective stakeholder enablement. What we can offer you Culture -We put our people first and prioritise the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Job Title: Packaging Officer  Department: Repair Operations  Reports to: Regional Repair Operations Manager  Location: Rivers - Port Harcourt Work Mode: Onsite Employment Type: Outsourcing About this role:  The Packaging Officer is responsible for ensuring all refurbished terminals that pass quality assurance (QA) are properly packaged, labelled, and logged before being sent to inventory for distribution. title: Product Design Manager - Design System
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial ecosystem, helping 10 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, and business management tools since 2019. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, it powers most of the country’s Point of Sale (POS) transactions. Through its subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes $22 billion monthly for its customers while operating profitably. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. About the role  Designing for money means designing for trust. Our customers are shop owners, traders and entrepreneurs, and many are new to digital products. They work on low-end devices and unreliable networks, where one confusing screen can cost them a sale. Your team's work has to hold up for them, whatever their ability or device. You make sure it does.  As a Design Manager, you'll lead a small team of product designers and be accountable for everything they ship: its quality, how it works as one product, and the results it drives for our customers and the business. Your team works either on the products our customers use on POS, mobile and web, or on the operational tools our teams use to serve them.  It is a hands-on role: you build the systems the team works within and step into the hardest problems yourself.  What you'll do  Set the design direction for your area, turn it into plans with milestones and measurable outcomes, and make the case for it to senior leaders in customer and business terms. Work with product partners so every designer begins from a clear, well-framed brief, and push back early when one isn't ready.  Keep each customer journey whole across teams, and resolve conflicting designs before they launch.  Run critique and design reviews against a definition of done that includes accessibility, and stay close enough to the work that nothing reaches customers below the bar. Decide what must be tested with customers before build and what can ship and be measured after, and plan that validation into delivery with success metrics defined up front. Make sure journeys use the design system, with market and product variations handled inside it rather than as one-off rebuilds. Plan and staff system contributions like any other project. Build trusted partnerships with product and engineering, so design shapes what gets built, and design and engineering stay in step through build.  Hire well, set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and build a growth path for each designer.  Bring AI tools into the team's design process, model effective and responsible use in your own work, and build that fluency across the team.  What you'll need to succeed  10+ years of experience in product design, with a portfolio of shipped work across mobile and web that shows the problem, your decisions and the results.  3+ years of experience managing product designers, including hiring, coaching and career development.  Experience setting design direction for a product area and leading a team to deliver it. Experience running a design quality practice, such as critique, design reviews and a definition of done, that raised the quality of shipped work.  Experience building shared patterns or templates adopted across teams, products or markets. Experience shipping accessible, inclusive products for people with disabilities, people new to digital products and people on limited devices and connectivity.  Experience using AI tools in design work and building that fluency across a team.  Nice to have  Experience designing for POS terminals is a strong plus. Experience in financial services, multiple markets or operational tools is also welcome.  What you will get: A leadership role in shaping the future of fintech - your work will impact millions of users. Career growth opportunities. A culture of experimentation - we encourage innovative thinking and rapid iteration. Competitive compensation and benefits. Remote-friendly work culture, with access to learning resources. What to expect in the hiring process  Recruiter conversation. Your background, what you want next, and practical details. 2. Case study review. Walk a design leader through one or two case studies in depth: one from your own work, one from a team you led.  Leadership challenge. Work through a product and team problem live with two design leaders.  Final interview. A conversation with the hiring manager. Why Join Us Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities. Fully remote work culture and support for professional development. What to expect in the hiring process Application & portfolio review: we assess your experience, leadership impact, and Design System case studies that demonstrate strategic thinking, process, and measurable outcomes. Preliminary phone call with recruiter: a brief conversation to discuss your background, leadership experience, and expectations. Interview with senior leadership: a deep dive into your leadership approach, design philosophy, and ability to drive impact. This includes a discussion on past projects and collaboration with cross-functional teams. Design leadership challenge: a scenario-based assessment to assess both strategic thinking and leadership skills while balancing UX/UI expertise. Final executive conversation: a discussion with senior leadership to assess alignment with our vision, strategic thinking, and team-building philosophy. How to apply: Submit your resume and portfolio showcasing your leadership in managing design teams, driving strategy, and delivering user-centred solutions with measurable business impact. We want to see case studies that demonstrate how you have led and developed designers, prioritised and managed projects, and fostered a high-performing team culture. Your portfolio should highlight how you have used research, data, and experimentation to inform decisions, optimise workflows, and drive success metrics.

title: Regional Lead, Client Implementation
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. What We Do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We leverage artificial intelligence and data-driven best practices to support our businesses, from providing credit and overdrafts to ensuring every transaction is secure. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out our stories on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. Job Purpose The Implementation Lead is responsible for building, managing, and continuously improving a high-performing regional team of Implementation agents. This role drives the strategic execution of Moniebook's customer onboarding programme at scale, ensuring that every new retail customer in the region is successfully activated, trained, and transitioned into a confident, long-term user of the Moniebook solution. Operating at the intersection of people leadership, operational excellence, and customer success strategy, the Implementation Lead sets performance standards, develops team capability, removes escalation blockers, and partners cross-functionally with Sales, Product, and Account Management to deliver a world-class onboarding experience. Success is measured by team-wide activation rates, time-to-value benchmarks, retention outcomes, and the quality of customer handoffs across the region measure success. Key Responsibilities Team Leadership & Performance Management Recruit, onboard, coach, and retain a regional team of Implementation Agents, fostering a culture of accountability, customer obsession, and continuous improvement. Set clear individual and team performance goals aligned to activation rates, time-to-value, feature adoption, CSAT scores, and churn reduction targets. Conduct regular 1:1s, team reviews, and performance evaluations; identify skill gaps and build development plans to close them. Onboarding Strategy & Programme Oversight Design scalable onboarding frameworks that allow the team to manage growing customer volumes without compromising on quality or personalisation. Define and maintain onboarding milestones, success metrics, and quality standards across all customer segments. Identify opportunities to streamline onboarding timelines and reduce time-to-value without sacrificing adoption depth. Escalation Management & Issue Resolution Act as the first point of escalation for complex technical issues, difficult customer situations, or onboarding stalls that agents are unable to resolve independently. Partner with Product, Engineering, and Support teams to drive resolution of systemic issues affecting onboarding outcomes across the region. Maintain clear escalation pathways and SLA standards, ensuring customers always feel supported and informed during issue resolution. Cross-functional Collaboration Partner closely with the Sales team to ensure smooth pre-to-post sale handoffs and that customer expectations are properly set before onboarding begins. Collaborate with Account Managers to refine the handoff process, ensuring agents provide complete, high-quality context that enables seamless long-term retention. Work with the Product team to surface recurring customer pain points, usability gaps, and feature adoption blockers, acting as a regional voice of the customer. Data, Reporting & Insights Track and analyse team-wide performance data including activation rates, onboarding completion timelines, feature adoption depth, CSAT scores, and early-stage churn metrics. Produce regular reports for senior leadership on regional onboarding health, trends, risks, and improvement initiatives. Use data to identify underperforming segments, agents, or onboarding touchpoints, and drive targeted interventions to address root causes. Process Improvement & Innovation Continuously review and refine onboarding processes, tools, and resources to improve efficiency, consistency, and customer outcomes. Champion the adoption of new technologies, automation, or methodologies that can enhance the team's ability to deliver high-touch onboarding at scale. Build a feedback loop between frontline agent insights and senior leadership/product decisions to ensure ground-level learnings influence the business. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Business, Technology, Operations, or a related field (or equivalent experience). 4 - 6 years of experience in customer onboarding, customer success, or implementation roles, with at least 2–3 years in a team lead or people management capacity. Proven track record of leading onboarding or CS teams to consistently achieve activation, adoption, and retention targets, ideally within SaaS, retail technology, or fintech. Strong people leadership skills with the ability to motivate, develop, and hold a distributed team accountable for outcomes. Excellent analytical skills, able to interpret customer health data, team performance metrics, and identify actionable trends. Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills; able to present to senior leadership, navigate cross-functional relationships, and represent the customer voice persuasively. Deep customer empathy combined with a results-driven orientation. Highly organised with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, projects, and escalations simultaneously without compromising quality. Comfortable working in fast-paced, ambiguous environments; brings structure and clarity without over-engineering. Preferred Qualifications Experience building or scaling onboarding teams from the ground up in a high-growth technology company. Exposure to retail operations, merchant services, or point-of-sale technology. Experience designing training curricula, onboarding playbooks, or knowledge management systems. Familiarity with customer health scoring methodologies, NPS/CSAT frameworks, or CS operations best practices. About You You are a natural leader who takes genuine pride in developing the people around you, and you measure your success by the success of your team and your customers. You are strategic and execution-focused; you can zoom out to design the right system and zoom in to resolve a customer escalation on the same day. You bring calm, clarity, and decisiveness under pressure. When things go wrong, your team looks to you and finds confidence, not panic. You are deeply data-literate; you use numbers to tell stories, make decisions, and hold yourself and your team accountable. You are a collaborative partner who builds trust across functions, Sales, Product, Support, and Account Management, and all see you as an ally, not a blocker. You thrive in environments where the playbook is still being written, and you take ownership of writing it. You are customer-obsessed at scale, even as you move further from direct customer interaction, you never lose sight of the human beings behind the metrics. What Success Looks Like Your regional team consistently achieves 90%+ customer activation rates within the 30–60 day onboarding window, month over month. Average time-to-live for customers in your region is at or below the 1–2 week target, with no systemic delays attributed to onboarding execution gaps. Regional post-onboarding CSAT scores average 4.5+, and your team's handoff quality is rated as excellent by Account Managers. Early-stage churn (within 90 days post-onboarding) for customers in your region remains below 5%. Your agents are among the most skilled and engaged at Moniebook, attrition on your team is low, development is visible, and performance is strong. You have documented, improved, and operationalised at least two significant enhancements to the regional onboarding playbook each quarter. What we can offer you Culture: We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning: We have a learning-and-development-focused environment, with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation: You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with the recruiter. An interview with the operations lead. A behavioural and technical interview with the business lead. Moniepoint is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out our stories on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. Job Purpose The Regional Security Lead ensures that our mission never stops. You are the guardian of our physical spaces, ensuring that every Moniepoint office is a sanctuary where our team can build and create without worry. By leading regional security operations, managing on-ground teams, and proactively identifying risks, you provide the stability and safety that allows financial happiness to thrive. You don't just react to incidents; you build the systems that prevent them. Key Responsibilities Safeguard our People and Assets: Lead the implementation of security policies that protect our team, offices, and equipment across your region. Master the Environment: Conduct regular security assessments to spot vulnerabilities and design innovative strategies to reduce risk. Lead the Front Line: Supervise and mentor private security guards and armed police personnel, ensuring they perform their duties with mastery and respect. Build Strong Alliances: Act as our primary liaison with law enforcement and emergency services, ensuring we always have a seat at the table during emergencies. Investigate and Solve: Lead the response to security breaches and accidents, providing clear, factual reports that help us learn and improve. Empower the Team: Design and deliver training programs that equip our security personnel and employees with life-saving protocols. Innovate for Safety: Stay ahead of security trends and technology (like CCTV and access control) to keep our regional operations modern and resilient. Support Business Resilience: Provide expert guidance on asset recovery and fraud investigation when the business needs your mastery. Qualifications Professional Background: Should have at least 5 years of experience successfully leading a security team in a guard services/physical security company or have 5 years of experience as an ex-commissioned service personnel supervisor—either in the military, police, or paramilitary. Education: A Bachelor’s degree in Criminology, Psychology, Criminal Justice, or a related field. Certification: You hold a recognized security certification such as CPP, PSP, or CPO. Integrity: A clean criminal record and the ability to pass a comprehensive background check are essential. Language & Culture: You speak the local dialects of the major tribes in your assigned region, allowing you to connect with the community. Good experience working with automated security systems like CCTV cameras, burglary alarm systems, etc. About You You are a Hero: You are driven by mastery and the desire to protect others. People count on you to come through when things get tough. You are Relatable: You don’t hide behind technical jargon. You communicate clearly and build trust with everyone, from the security guards to the executive team. You are Proactive: You don’t wait for things to go wrong. You have the "Creator" spirit, always looking for better ways to secure our future.  You are composed: In high-pressure situations, you are the calmest person in the room. You lead with facts, not emotions. What Success Looks Like Zero Preventable Incidents: Our regional offices remain safe, secure, and fully operational. High Readiness: Security personnel are well-trained and respond to drills or real-world events with 100% precision. Strong Community Ties: You have built a network of local stakeholders that helps Moniepoint navigate regional risks effectively. Operational Excellence: Security technology is 100% functional, and documentation is factual, honest, and actionable. What we can offer you Culture: We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all voices are heard, and we look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning: We have a learning- and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing and training. Compensation: You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, and an annual bonus, plus other benefits. Moniepoint Inc. is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Senior Principal, Talent Marketing
description: About us Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times as Africa's fastest-growing fintech, Moniepoint is trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of dollars in transactions monthly. About this role As our Senior Principal, Talent Marketing, you will be the strategic architect responsible for establishing Moniepoint's talent brand and candidate pipeline in new markets from scratch. Where Moniepoint is not yet an established consumer brand, you will solve complex talent acquisition problems by understanding how senior engineers, engineering managers, and technical leaders think, connect, and evaluate career moves across Europe. Working from a blank piece of paper with high autonomy, you will translate our global Employer Value Proposition (EVP) into localized, high-converting talent marketing strategies. End-to-End Pipeline Activation: Ensure events are never vanity exercises; architect end-to-end follow-up systems and talent nurture funnels that convert event attendees into active, screened pipelines for our TA partners. Developer Platform Immersion: Leverage deep knowledge of where engineers consume information (e.g., GitLab/GitHub communities, tech forums, Discord/Slack groups, Meetup, Eventbrite) to drive authentic engagement. 3. Strategic Hiring Campaigns & Technical Enablement Targeted Campaign Architecture: Partner with TA leads and Engineering Directors to identify acute hiring bottlenecks and build agile, multi-channel marketing campaigns that address specialized, hard-to-fill tech disciplines. Technical EVP Translation: Translate technical architecture, distributed systems challenges, and fintech infrastructure realities into authentic, intellectually rigorous technical messaging that outshines local competitors. Recruiter Enablement & Narrative Toolkits: Equip our technical sourcing and recruitment teams with high-leverage narrative assets—outbound pitch decks, technical one-pagers, culture collateral, and messaging sequences that double recruiter outreach conversion. 4. Performance, Analytics & Optimization Hiring-Centric Metrics: Discard vanity metrics. Evaluate every initiative against pipeline contribution, qualified applicant rates, candidate quality score, cost-per-hire, and time-to-fill. Budget Oversight: Own and allocate dedicated talent marketing budgets with extreme commercial discipline—scaling programs that drive measurable hires and rapidly decommissioning initiatives that underdeliver. Paid Acquisition (Tactical Lever): Oversee and strategically deploy paid recruitment marketing spend across relevant technical platforms and channels when targeted outbound and community channels require acceleration. 5. Strategic Leadership & Scalability Strategic Thought Partnership: Serve as the trusted advisor to the Head of Talent Acquisition, VP of Engineering, and Brand Leadership on talent market intelligence, competitor positioning, and developer sentiment. Playbook Documentation: Establish and document Moniepoint's global talent expansion playbook, creating scalable frameworks that will be deployed across future international markets. European Market Expertise: Demonstrated experience building talent brand presence and hiring pipelines across European tech ecosystems (particularly Central/Eastern Europe such as Poland, and Western/Southern Europe such as the UK or Spain). Zero-to-One Market Entry Track Record: Proven success entering new geographies or scaling talent brand where the employer brand was nascent or non-existent, creating playbooks from a blank sheet of paper. Fintech & Scale Exposure: Experience in hyper-growth fintech, high-frequency/payments infrastructure, or high-scale distributed systems environments. International Collaboration: Experience collaborating with international founding teams or distributed tech hubs across emerging and mature markets. Skills & Competencies Mastery in Event-Driven Pipeline Activation: Extensive hands-on experience designing and executing physical and digital developer events and architecting the subsequent candidate nurturing journey that yields hires. Deep Engineering Domain Fluency: Genuine understanding of software engineering culture, tech stacks (distributed systems, backend, infra, DevOps), and developer channels (Meetup, Eventbrite, GitLab/GitHub, Reddit, tech conferences). Comfort with Substantial Ambiguity: High agency and entrepreneurial drive; ability to make decisive bets, test hypotheses, and build structure in fast-moving, high-growth environments. Strategic Campaign Design: Ability to connect high-level EVP strategy to pragmatic, sprint-based talent acquisition sprints that deliver on an aggressive hiring plan (500+ tech hires). Paid Digital Campaign Optimization: Direct experience running and optimizing paid digital recruitment advertising campaigns independently across social and developer networks. What success looks like in this role First 30 Days (Discovery & Immersion): Map the competitive landscape and developer talent dynamics in Poland and Spain. Establish alignment with technical hiring leads (PEP, Engineering Directors) and TA leads to define immediate priority pipelines. Audit existing employer brand collateral and identify localized messaging gaps for European tech hiring. First 90 Days (Initial Market Entry & Quick Wins): Launch the first pilot physical event / developer meetup presence in Poland with a complete post-event pipeline conversion funnel. Roll out the European Recruiter Enablement Toolkit (localized pitch decks, outreach sequences, and technical one-pagers). Launch targeted marketing sprints for top 3 hardest-to-fill senior technical roles. Consistently contribute qualified, pre-warmed candidate pipelines directly supporting the ramp toward 500 tech/product hires. Prove multi-channel attribution showing which community and marketing initiatives are yielding quality hires. Measurably decrease time-to-fill and increase direct outbound response rates across all European technical roles. Solidify Moniepoint's reputation as an employer of choice for Europe's most ambitious engineers. Why join us High-Impact Mission: Play a career-defining role in building the engineering backbone of Africa's fastest-growing fintech as it scales globally. True Ownership & Dedicated Resources: Autonomy to build from scratch with dedicated budget backing and direct executive sponsorship. title: Senior Product Designer (UX)
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions.
